pieces.title: Being in Juvie
pieces.author: a young person at Clark Children & Family Justice Center
pieces.text:
It’s cold and dark 
when you first go in. 
People’s looking at you 
as an inmate, 
like you’re a dangerous person. 
I get cold and shivers 
down my spine. 
 
I can feel anxiety 
coming by 
when they first 
take me in my room. 
I feel cold and depressed. 
I can only see these white walls 
every time I turn. 
 
I can only think to myself, 
what have I done to be in here? 
 
I miss being with my family and my friends. 
I miss having a hug from my mom, the warmth like a fire. 
I miss being outside every day, playing Uno with my friends. 
I miss steak, with greens. 
I miss being around the house playing ball with my dog. 
I miss having to sit on the porch and seeing the days go by. 
 
When I’m in juvie
I can’t see myself outside anymore. 
Judges keep telling me I’m a menace to society  
or not a good person, 
but I know that I am. 
I’m a good person. 
I’m a loving person. 
I just miss my family and being out. 

Now every time I go out of my room I just feel a deep cold. 
It feels like winter with frostbite on your hands. 
I just sit around the table watching people go by. 
It feels like years have passed since I sat down. 
 
I sit around and think about how I miss my family. 
Playing games. 
Having fun. 
Hearing my mom laugh 
and my family and my siblings. 
 
I love my life. 
I know I’m a good person.

pieces.title: The Family That Pays Together
pieces.author: Daniel Mustard
pieces.caption: Daniel Mustard is currently incarcerated at WSP
pieces.pageText:
These children have just parted ways with their incarcerated dads. Visiting a parent in prison can be both joyful and painful. The famous Corcoran Mama photo from the book that I've recreated here haunts me because of all the love trapped inside those walls. This was a hard painting for me to finish. For kids, the visit offers a few precious hours of connection, but leaving means walking away while their parent remains behind, carrying both the warmth of the visit and the pain of separation.

— Daniel Mustard

pieces.title: Fly
pieces.author: produced by inmates currently incarcerated at WSP
pieces.text:
Give me wings so I can fly. Music is the language of my life. And it's mine so I-
Can't decline. Give me wings so I can-
Give me the bars, give me the love, give me the juice I need. Uh-huh. Flying the skies, walking on water, I'm a winged steed. The language of life that I speak is older than human speech. Digging in music, that's my freedom, how else can I breathe?
Visions of a prisoner, watch my time fly. Because it's hard to see our struggles from a blind eye. It's emotions in every note, the power from the quotes, 'cause speaking of our hope will make the mind cry.
Fly. Fly. Never thought I'd see this in my life. Used to put the 30 with the Sprite and kept it on me for the slide. But now I thrive to see myself in different lights, different levels, different heights.
This atmosphere is getting tight. Top is lonely. Break the door down for the homies. Say I'm wrong, you gonna have to show me. But a slight departure from the old me. If you know me, then you know me. Thief in the night with no codeine. Keeping it tight with all my proceeds. Still in the game and steady growing.
I'm from the pavement. The judge sentenced me to greatness. Real Macky never stop, education fueling my patience. I talk less, I say more. Uh-huh, that's player maintenance. I'm from the tuck, I stay fly. You feel me? Can't be complacent. Can't settle, my ticket's platinum, I'm elevated. It's major ripple when I splash, I got them all concentrated.
My swag still loud like a jet, I stay elevated. I'm still praying for my brothers, I hope that they all gon' make it.
I made some new friends today. Chatting up 'bout neuropathways. Rewiring, seeing changes, so astounded. I love it, love it, love it, love it, love on sweet influence. It was a pleasure on behalf of Jake and Kevin Yeans.
Give me wings so I can fly. Music is the language of my life. And it's mine so I decide. And it's a call I can't decline, so I go.
Time is now. Be here. What now? Every day it's always do, go, stop, slow. Done getting lost looking through the back, the past. Looking for the who's who, what was. Year after year walking in this life of love.
Tear after tear tripping in this fog of a drug. Mask off. Pass the fall and the ball. Mask off. Pass the pounds and the fake love. Show me real, give me a hug. Sky's clearing, mind's free. It's my life. Give me wings so I can fly. Music is the language of my life.
Can't decline.
And start all over again. I wanna be a better husband. I wanna be a better dad. I wanna be a better brother. I wanna be a better man. All the words in my heart that I should never speak. On a plateau chasing goals that I could never reach. Learn my lesson, life's a blessing, what I'm tryna teach.
My mom's expectations all I'm tryna meet.
My mental health, my mental wealth. Music keeps me going, helps me be myself. Without music, where would I be? Might as well be a statue or a tree. No matter where you come from or who you are, music connects people, don't need a car. It's the language of love, the language of life.
It's hella old, like the blessings from Christ.
Give me wings so I can fly. Music is the language of my life. And it's mine so I decide. And it's a call I can't decline. Give me wings so I can-
Stronger than ever before. Craving for a beat, I wanna hear more. Bass hits hard, better shut the door. Anxiety is gone, I evened up the score.
Harsh desire, lyrics spitting fire. I may be old, but refuse to retire. Words are like venom and toxic like a stream. Balance on the edge, but feels like a dream. Give me wings so I can fly, fly, fly.
I'm easily distracted, I'm hyperreactive. Attention deficient, convicted, indecent. I'm far from my target, I run this department. I sing from my heart in my eight-foot apartment.
My emotions jumping through hurdles, I can't find the finish. Crying these tears, feeling unsafe, it started to blur my vision. Been seeking for help for so damn long, this shit must be in the Guinness. I'm sharing the story of my life and hoping that y'all will listen.
In the morning when I wake, my mind races. How did I survive these decades in these places? Guess that life I lived in here took inner patience. I wore my heart out on my sleeve and not two faces.
Yeah. Fly away like a kite in the sky. Levitating to a new place, Marty McFly. We don't change, but we heal if we finally decide. Free my mind from this prison, I'm a light in the sky.
Give me wings so I can fly. Music is the language of my life.
Give me wings so I can fly. Let me spread my wings so I can fly. Far away from here, never looking back in time. Time, we can't get it back. Moving forward, never backwards, so sit back and just relax. Took a melody, it turned into this song. Rock this class in SPL never did me any harm.
In lieu of giving you a lyrical Louisiana lullaby, I'm more misinformed to manipulate your mind.
When wittingly and whimsically we ask for a rewind, I'm forced to flee and fanatically find the wings that I need to fly.
